financials_interim.notes: Source: NAMU Interim Financial Statements for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 (PDF pp.2-9, filed 12 Aug 2026, cdn.cse.lk/cmt/upload_report_file/725_1786618707218.pdf). Single-entity filing -- only one column of figures is presented (no separate Group/Company split), so per project convention this is entered as a single GROUP row. Operating_profit is NOT an explicit line item in NAMU's P&L format (structure is Gross Profit -> Other Income -> Change in FV of Biological Assets -> Admin Expenses -> Management Fee -> Finance Cost -> Finance Income -> Share of JV Profit -> PBT); it is derived here as Gross Profit + Other Income - Admin Expenses - Management Fee = 624,515 + 24,473 - 63,538 - 107,747 = 477,703 (pre-finance, pre-JV operating measure; excludes finance income/cost and share of JV profit which NAMU reports below this line). Short/long-term borrowings are 0 -- NAMU carries only lease liabilities (Rs.6,039k current / Rs.796,704k non-current per BS, p.2), no interest-bearing bank debt, and no overdraft. Capex of Rs.2,913k is 'Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment' per the cash flow statement (p.5); NAMU separately discloses 'Investments in Immature plantation' of Rs.27,530k (biological-asset capex, not included in the capex field to keep it comparable to the PPE-only convention used elsewhere in this DB) -- both are captured in cash_from_investing (net Rs.12,828k, which also includes Rs.43,083k dividend received from the JV and Rs.188k grants received). EPS basic 2.12 = PAT 504,433k / weighted avg shares 237,500,001 (post 1:10 subdivision effected in 2025/26, comparatives restated) -- cross-checked, consistent. No diluted EPS disclosed separately (no dilutive instruments); eps_diluted left null. Segment note (p.8) shows revenue split Tea Rs.340,424k / Rubber Rs.25,324k / Oil Palm Rs.924,336k / Coconut Rs.15,449k / Cinnamon Rs.548k -- Oil Palm is by far the dominant crop (70.8% of revenue) and grew 14.2% YoY (Rs.809,655k -> Rs.924,336k); Tea revenue fell 15.0% YoY (Rs.400,484k -> Rs.340,424k). Balance sheet identity checks: Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity (15,896,667 = 3,505,079 + 12,391,588, exact). PBT - Tax = PAT check: 677,553 - 173,120 = 504,433, exact.

thesis.thesis_text: Namunukula Plantations PLC (NAMU) is a diversified Sri Lankan plantation company increasingly concentrated in Oil Palm, which grew to 70.8% of Group revenue this quarter (from 64.3% a year earlier) on 14.2% YoY segment revenue growth to Rs.924.3mn, more than offsetting a 15.0% decline in Tea revenue. Group revenue grew 3.6% YoY to Rs.1,306.1mn, but Gross Profit fell 2.3% because Oil Palm's own cost base grew 46.0% YoY, outpacing its revenue growth -- a margin-compression trend within the Group's fastest-growing crop that the filing does not attribute to a specific cause (e.g., fertiliser or fruit-purchase-price inflation). PAT still rose 7.0% YoY to Rs.504.4mn, helped by a 17.3% rise in finance income (on the Group's large ~Rs.7.5bn cash and investment balance) and a 24.1% rise in joint-venture profit share, both sitting below the operating line. The balance sheet is debt-free and highly liquid (current ratio 10.07x), and at Rs.67.00 the stock trades at an approximate 7.9x run-rate P/E and 1.25x P/B -- statistically cheap. However, the dividend yield case is unreliable: the FY2025 DPS of Rs.15.00 on file appears to predate NAMU's 1:10 share subdivision, and if not itself adjusted, would overstate yield roughly 10-fold at the current, post-subdivision share count. With only one interim quarter on file, no annual report, and this dividend-data ambiguity unresolved, this thesis should be treated as preliminary (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id manual_3931ee9092a621c4, p.3 and p.8).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no palm oil/tea commodity-price or Sri Lanka plantation-sector data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period trend), the FY2023-FY2025 dividend figures on file appear inconsistent with NAMU's 1:10 share subdivision and could not be confirmed as subdivision-adjusted, and the filing gives no explanation for the 46.0% YoY cost growth in the Oil Palm segment.

financial_quality.rationale: Namunukula Plantations PLC (NAMU) has a strong, debt-free balance sheet: short-term and long-term borrowings are both zero (only lease liabilities of Rs.802.7mn), total equity of Rs.12,391.6mn against total liabilities of just Rs.3,505.1mn (Debt/Equity ~0.28x, entirely lease-related), and a current ratio of 10.07x (current assets Rs.8,938.7mn / current liabilities Rs.887.4mn) including Rs.7,489.5mn of cash and short-term investments. Quarterly ROE is approximately 4.1% (annualised ~16.3%). However, Gross Profit fell 2.3% YoY to Rs.624.5mn despite revenue growth, because Oil Palm -- now 70.8% of Group revenue -- saw its own segment cost base grow 46.0% YoY (Rs.180,972k to Rs.264,281k), outpacing its 14.2% revenue growth; PBT growth (+1.4%) was preserved only by a 17.3% rise in Finance Income and a 24.1% rise in Joint Venture profit share, both below the operating line.

growth_outlook.rationale: Revenue grew 3.6% YoY to Rs.1,306.1mn, driven almost entirely by Oil Palm (+14.2% to Rs.924.3mn, now 70.8% of Group revenue vs 64.3% a year earlier), which more than offset a 15.0% decline in Tea revenue (Rs.400.5mn to Rs.340.4mn) and a halving of Tea's gross profit (-54.2%). Operating profit itself fell 5.4% YoY (per the derived operating_profit metric), and Group gross profit fell 2.3% because Oil Palm's own cost base grew faster than its revenue -- the headline PAT growth (+7.0%) is therefore driven more by non-crop items (finance income, JV profit share, lower tax) than by improving crop-level profitability, and the Group's rising concentration in a single crop (Oil Palm) is a trend worth monitoring.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.67.00 (2026-08-31, market cap Rs.15,485.0mn), annualising this quarter's EPS (Rs.2.12 x4 = Rs.8.48) implies a P/E of approximately 7.9x, and P/B is approximately 1.25x on equity of Rs.12,391.6mn -- statistically cheap on both measures for a debt-free, cash-rich company. The dividends table shows a DPS of Rs.15.00 for FY2025 (Rs.13.00 FY2024, Rs.14.00 FY2023), but these figures likely predate NAMU's 1:10 share subdivision executed in FY2025/26 (per the interim filing's own EPS restatement) -- if not itself adjusted for the 10x increase in shares outstanding, a naive yield calculation (~22% at the current price) would be overstated roughly 10-fold; a subdivision-adjusted DPS of roughly Rs.1.50 would imply a more plausible ~2.2% yield. This discrepancy could not be resolved from the data on file and should not be relied upon without confirming whether the dividends table is subdivision-adjusted.
citations: dividends: FY2025 DPS 15.00, FY2024 DPS 13.00, FY2023 DPS 14.00 (pre/post-subdivision basis unconfirmed)

business_quality.rationale: NAMU is a diversified plantation company (Tea, Rubber, Oil Palm, Coconut, Cinnamon) that has become increasingly concentrated in Oil Palm (70.8% of revenue this quarter, up from 64.3% a year earlier) -- a crop with different price/cost dynamics than Tea, and a segment whose own cost base grew 46.0% YoY this quarter without an explained driver in the filing. The Group carries longstanding, unresolved litigation over estate employees' statutory dues (30 cases across two Magistrates Courts, one High Court case won with an appeal pending, 29 others awaiting a higher-court date) -- a legacy contingent-liability overhang common to Sri Lankan plantation companies, not unique to NAMU, and not quantified as a current-period P&L driver.

governance_risk.rationale: NAMU has a three-year dividend track record on file (though the pre/post-subdivision basis is unconfirmed, as noted above), a mild governance positive. The Note 8 litigation on estate employees' statutory dues has been ongoing across multiple prior periods with no new quantified impact this quarter, suggesting the company treats it as a stable, disclosed contingent liability rather than an escalating risk. No disclosures/circulars feed exists in this project to independently verify board or ownership changes.

key_reasons: Debt-free balance sheet (zero short/long-term borrowings, only lease liabilities) with a 10.07x current ratio and Rs.7,489.5mn of cash and investments -- one of the strongest balance sheets reviewed in this batch

Revenue growth (+3.6% YoY) is driven almost entirely by Oil Palm (+14.2%, now 70.8% of Group revenue), but Oil Palm's own cost base grew 46.0% YoY, faster than its revenue, and Group gross profit fell 2.3% despite the revenue growth -- PAT growth (+7.0%) instead came from a 17.3% rise in finance income and a 24.1% rise in JV profit share, both below the operating line

At ~7.9x run-rate P/E and ~1.25x P/B, valuation looks statistically cheap, but the dividend yield case is unreliable: the FY2025 DPS of Rs.15.00 likely predates NAMU's 1:10 share subdivision and, if unadjusted, would overstate yield roughly 10-fold
watch_factors: Oil Palm segment cost base grew 46.0% YoY, outpacing its 14.2% revenue growth -- if this cost pressure continues while Oil Palm keeps growing as a share of revenue (now 70.8%), Group gross margin could keep compressing even as the top line grows
Tea segment revenue fell 15.0% YoY and its gross profit halved (-54.2%) -- a second crop under pressure that is being masked by Oil Palm's growth at the Group level

Dividend data (FY2023-FY2025 DPS of Rs.13-15) appears inconsistent with NAMU's 1:10 share subdivision executed in FY2025/26 -- confirm whether these figures are subdivision-adjusted before relying on any yield calculation
Longstanding litigation on estate employees' statutory dues (30 cases, Note 8) remains unresolved -- a legacy contingent liability to monitor, though unchanged and unquantified this quarter

horizon_notes.6m: Q2 FY2026/27 results will show whether Oil Palm's cost inflation (46.0% YoY this quarter) persists and whether Tea's decline stabilises or continues.
horizon_notes.1y: If Oil Palm can convert its revenue growth into gross-profit growth (rather than cost growth outpacing revenue), the Group's crop-level profitability trend would strengthen; continued cost pressure would keep PAT growth dependent on finance income and JV profit share, which are less predictable.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on how NAMU manages an increasingly Oil-Palm-concentrated crop mix (70.8% of revenue) through commodity price and cost cycles, which cannot yet be tested with only one quarter on file.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/commodity-price data source exists in this project to assess global palm oil and tea price trends relevant to NAMU's multi-year crop-mix trajectory.

interim_updates.note_text: Namunukula Plantations PLC (NAMU) reported revenue of Rs.1,306.1mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 3.6% YoY from Rs.1,260.2mn, driven almost entirely by Oil Palm: segmental revenue (p.8 note) grew 14.2% YoY to Rs.924.3mn (from Rs.809.7mn), which more than offset a 15.0% YoY decline in Tea revenue (Rs.400.5mn to Rs.340.4mn) -- crop-mix data shows Oil Palm is now 70.8% of total revenue versus 64.3% a year earlier. Gross profit fell 2.3% YoY to Rs.624.5mn (from Rs.638.8mn) despite the revenue growth, because Oil Palm's own segment revenue expenditure rose faster than its revenue (Rs.180,972k to Rs.264,281k, +46.0%), compressing that segment's own margin even as its gross profit still grew 4.6% (Rs.581,448k to Rs.608,432k, p.8); Tea swung from a Rs.57,791k gross profit to Rs.26,466k (-54.2%) on the revenue decline. Profit before tax was broadly flat, up 1.4% YoY to Rs.677.6mn (from Rs.668.4mn), because two below-gross-profit items offset the weaker operating result: Finance Income rose 17.3% YoY to Rs.153.4mn (from Rs.130.7mn, on the Group's large ~Rs.7.5bn cash and investment balance) and the Company's Share of Profit from the Joint Venture (Kelani Valley Canopy/RPC-related JV) rose 24.1% YoY to Rs.73.6mn (from Rs.59.3mn). Tax expense fell 12.2% YoY to Rs.173.1mn (from Rs.197.2mn), so profit after tax rose 7.0% YoY to Rs.504.4mn (from Rs.471.3mn), and basic EPS rose to Rs.2.12 from Rs.1.98 (both restated for the 2025/26 1:10 share subdivision). Other income fell sharply, down 36.3% YoY to Rs.24.5mn (from Rs.38.4mn), a small absolute drag. No wage-cost/regulatory commentary specific to this quarter is disclosed beyond the ongoing Note 8 litigation on estate employees' statutory dues (30 cases at Magistrates Courts Passara/Bandarawela against Tusker Bottling Co and the sub-leased estates' Superintendents; Company won HC Badulla case 59/2015, Labour Commissioner's appeal pending; the other 29 cases await a higher-court date, arguments concluded, judgment reserved) -- unchanged from the prior period and not a quantified P&L driver this quarter.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for NAMU in this database, so no prior quarter (Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column (three months ended 30 June 2025) is used. Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) NAMU's P&L format has no explicit 'Operating Profit' line -- it goes straight from Gross Profit/Other Income/Admin/Management Fee to Finance Income/Cost to Share of JV Profit to PBT, so operating_profit in financial_statements is a derived figure (Gross Profit + Other Income - Admin Expenses - Management Fee), not a number NAMU itself discloses; (2) the filing gives no rubber/oil-palm/coconut yield or price commentary beyond the bare segmental revenue/cost table -- no explanation is given for why Oil Palm's own cost base grew 46.0% (e.g. no mention of fertilizer, fuel, or FFB purchase price inflation), so this could not be attributed to a specific named cost driver; (3) no plantation wage/regulatory commentary specific to this quarter (e.g. a government-mandated wage revision) is disclosed -- gratuity expense by segment is shown but not explained; (4) the Rs.70,690k FVTOCI loss in other comprehensive income (financial assets) is not explained further.
interim_updates.takeaway: Revenue grew 3.6% YoY to Rs.1,306.1mn almost entirely on Oil Palm, whose segment revenue rose 14.2% YoY to Rs.924.3mn (70.8% of Group revenue, up from 64.3%) and offset a 15.0% YoY fall in Tea revenue. Gross profit still fell 2.3% YoY because Oil Palm's own revenue expenditure grew 46.0% faster than its revenue, compressing margin even as its gross profit rose. PBT ended up only marginally higher (+1.4%) than gross profit would suggest, because a 17.3% YoY rise in finance income (Rs.153.4mn, on the Group's large cash pile) and a 24.1% rise in JV profit share (Rs.73.6mn) sit below the operating line and cushioned the weaker crop margin. PAT rose 7.0% YoY to Rs.504.4mn, helped further by a 12.2% fall in tax expense.
operational_highlights: Revenue up 3.6% YoY to Rs.1,306.1mn (from Rs.1,260.2mn); Oil Palm segment revenue +14.2% YoY to Rs.924.3mn (from Rs.809.7mn), now 70.8% of Group revenue vs 64.3% a year earlier (segment note, p.8)
Tea segment revenue fell 15.0% YoY to Rs.340.4mn (from Rs.400.5mn); Tea segment gross profit fell 54.2% to Rs.26.5mn (from Rs.57.8mn)

Oil Palm segment revenue expenditure rose 46.0% YoY (Rs.180,972k to Rs.264,281k), faster than its 14.2% revenue growth -- gross profit for the segment still grew 4.6% to Rs.608.4mn but on a thinner margin
Group gross profit fell 2.3% YoY to Rs.624.5mn (from Rs.638.8mn) despite higher revenue, on the Oil Palm cost pressure and the Tea decline

Finance income up 17.3% YoY to Rs.153.4mn (from Rs.130.7mn); Share of profit from Joint Venture up 24.1% YoY to Rs.73.6mn (from Rs.59.3mn) -- both below-gross-profit items that offset the weaker crop margin and lifted PBT
PBT up 1.4% YoY to Rs.677.6mn; tax expense down 12.2% YoY to Rs.173.1mn; PAT up 7.0% YoY to Rs.504.4mn; basic EPS Rs.2.12 (from Rs.1.98, restated for the 1:10 share subdivision)
Other income fell 36.3% YoY to Rs.24.5mn (from Rs.38.4mn) -- a modest absolute drag

Legal proceedings on employees' statutory dues (Note 8, p.6) remain outstanding -- 30 cases at Magistrates Courts Passara/Bandarawela; Company won HC Badulla case 59/2015 (Labour Commissioner's appeal pending); 29 other cases awaiting a higher-court date, judgment reserved -- unchanged status, no new quantified impact this quarter
key_drivers: Oil Palm segment revenue +14.2% YoY to Rs.924.3mn (from Rs.809.7mn, segment note p.8) was the single largest driver of Group revenue growth, now 70.8% of total revenue

Oil Palm segment revenue expenditure rose 46.0% YoY (Rs.180,972k to Rs.264,281k) -- outpacing the segment's own revenue growth and the main reason Group gross profit fell 2.3% YoY despite higher revenue
Tea segment revenue -15.0% YoY (Rs.400.5mn to Rs.340.4mn) and Tea gross profit -54.2% (Rs.57.8mn to Rs.26.5mn) -- second-largest drag on the gross profit line

Finance income +17.3% YoY (Rs.130.7mn to Rs.153.4mn) and Share of JV profit +24.1% YoY (Rs.59.3mn to Rs.73.6mn) together added Rs.37.6mn versus the prior year, the main reason PBT still rose 1.4% despite the weaker gross margin
